study type: Cross-sectional survey with a mother-infant cohort component
exposure: parabens (methyl paraben (MP), ethyl paraben (EP), propyl paraben (PP), iso-propyl paraben, butyl paraben, iso-butyl paraben)
bisphenols (bisphenol A (BPA), bisphenol F, bisphenol S, bisphenol AF, bisphenol Z)
cohort: The study included breast milk samples from mothers across 20 cities in China, and paired breast milk and urine samples from mothers and their breastfed infants in a cohort from Hangzhou, China.
finding: The research revealed extensive exposure of Chinese infants to endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) via breast milk, with MP, TCS, and BPA identified as having the highest cumulative endocrine disruption risk intensities.
